messages:
olivia: Heads-up — sketch for an 'slab' coexistence approach for v2/v3 endpoints. Idea: partition tenants into deterministic slabs, route slabs to either v2 or v3, keep the runtime and client contract stable, avoid global shims. High-level: hashing, header routing, telemetry + escape hatch.

sam: Sounds promising. How do we choose slab granularity? per-tenant or range buckets?

ravi: Proposal: hash(tenant_id) % 100 -> slab 0..99. Start with 1% slabs (one slab = 1 tenant-hash percent) for canary, double every 24h if stable. Pros: predictable capacity slices; cons: can fragment batching and caches.

kevin: Major concern: KV/prefix cache thrash when many tenants move across slabs. Warmup required or we pay latency spike.

olivia: Agreed. Plan: attach an internal header `X-Redwood-Slab: <id>` so caches can get affinity, and run a pre-warm replay job against the target slab before switching traffic.

emmie: Telemetry: we need slab_id, tenant_id, model_version, latency, 5xx rate. Abort rollout if error_rate > 2% vs baseline over a 10m window. Also track tail latency (p99).

sam: SDK question — do we expose slab header or keep it gateway-internal? I prefer internal only.

olivia: Keep it internal. SDKs should expose an opt-in version flag (e.g., `client.withApiVersion('v3')`) but the gateway decides routing. That avoids client manipulation and accidental bypass.

kevin: Also add a capacity gate: only enable slab if capacity headroom > 20% and model RT < SLO + 10ms. Otherwise fallback to v2.

ravi: Edge case: cross-tenant workflows (calls that fan-out to other tenants) can hit mixing problems. For those, consider sticky routing: pin the origin tenant's slab for the duration of the workflow.

olivia: Example envoy route snippet for slab header routing:```
- match:
    headers:
      - name: X-Redwood-Slab
        exact_match: "17"
  route:
    cluster: model-v3-cluster
```

emmie: We'll also need a lightweight audit log for slab assignments + a runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbook/slab-design — include rollback steps and the abort criteria.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy succeeded for slab 01 -> v3 in us-west at 4790123500 :rocket:

kevin: Nice. After canary we should run a churn test (high QPS small payloads) to see cache behaviour.

olivia: Decision checklist I'm putting together: hash function, initial canary slab(s)=1%, warmup replay, telemetry metrics + abort rule, capacity gating, header routing (internal), sticky routing for cross-tenant workflows, SDK opt-in signal only. I'll draft an RFC + careful rollout playbook (prewarm jobs, canary gates, automated rollback).

sam: Please @oncall once the RFC has rollout gates. Also cc @security for any header leakage concerns.

olivia: Will do. Thanks all — I'll post the RFC tomorrow and link the playbook. :white_check_mark:
